P-13-chetyre-bloka.текст: A single ultra-premium cinematic frame in 16:9 landscape at 1920 by 1080 pixels, built like the cover of a business quarterly and not like a slide: a precise axonometric cutaway, thirty degree isometric projection with no perspective distortion, of four industrial blocks standing side by side on a dark polished ground plane, each block a real building volume with concrete walls, exposed steel portal frames, a roof partly cut away to show the interior, and its own sectional roll-up loading gate on the front face with a rubber bumper, a bollard and a shallow ramp. The four volumes grow in exact visible proportion from left to right so that size is read by the eye before it is read by any numeral: the second block is one third larger in footprint than the first, the third is twice the first, and the fourth is four times the first and clearly the tallest, its portal frame reaching roughly twice the height of the smallest block and carrying an overhead crane beam. Scale is made physical by the ground itself, which is engraved with a fine surveyed grid of equal square modules cut into the concrete, so a viewer can literally count modules under each block and see the footprints stack up; a hairline dimension line with arrowheads at both ends runs along the front edge of every block, and each block casts a correct hard shadow onto that engraved grid. The infographic lives inside the scene as manufactured hardware, never as a pasted overlay: in front of each block, set into the floor, lies a brushed steel plate flush with the concrete, bolted at the corners, and the area figure is deep-engraved into that plate with a machined V groove that catches the key light and holds a thin line of shadow. The four engraved figures read exactly «180 м²», «240 м²», «360 м²» and «720 м²», one under each block from left to right in that order, all four set in dense condensed technical sans at a capital height of about four percent of the frame height, all four sharing one perfect common baseline, all four centred on the vertical axis of their own block, with the superscript two rendered correctly as a raised numeral. The headline is a cinematic title card lying on the same floor plane, obeying the axonometric projection, painted into the floor marking as crisp warm white lettering with slightly worn edges where forklifts have crossed it: the exact inscription «СВОБОДНЫ ЧЕТЫРЕ БЛОКА» placed across the upper left of the frame on a single line with no hyphenation, capital height about eleven percent of the frame height, wide letter tracking, the largest element in the whole image, its baseline receding with the floor perspective yet still reading flat and instantly legible. Geometry is strict and measured: a twelve column grid with five percent outer margins and an eight unit baseline grid, the headline occupying columns one through seven, the four blocks seated on a single shared ground line across columns one through twelve with equal gutters of exactly one grid module between neighbouring blocks, each engraved plate inset half a module from its block face, and a guaranteed clear space of at least two and a half percent of the frame height around every text element so that no figure touches a wall, a shadow, a dimension line or the frame edge, and nothing overlaps or is clipped. The palette is locked to five hexadecimal values and no other colour exists anywhere in the frame, including reflections on the polished floor, gate paint, bumpers, machinery and spill light: amber #E8A400 as the sole accent, used for the light spilling out of the open gates, the engraved grooves and the dimension arrowheads; muted gold #C9A233 for secondary reflections on steel and on the brushed plates; graphite #14171C for concrete volumes and gate slats; ink black #0E1116 for the surrounding void, the ground falloff and the deep shadows; warm white #F5F1E8 for lit roof edges, hairlines, floor marking and all type. No blue, no green, no red, no safety yellow, no neon, no cyberpunk glow, no colour grading outside these five values. Lighting is cinematic and directional: a single hard amber key from the upper left at about forty degrees carves the block volumes, skims the engraved floor grid at a low grazing angle so every groove is legible, throws four long parallel hard-edged shadows to the lower right, and falls off into black at the frame margins, while a very faint warm white ambient keeps the cutaway interiors readable and a thin haze of dust hangs in the gate light. Large-format architectural rendering look, corrected verticals, deep depth of field, fine film grain, matte finish, no flare, no vignette. Absolutely no additional text, no captions, no unit labels beyond those given, no door numbers, no watermarks, no logos, no invented words, no Latin transliteration, no gibberish letterforms; only the inscriptions specified here, reproduced character by character with exact Cyrillic spelling, exact digits and exact spacing. The headline must stay fully legible when the frame is scaled to a small feed thumbnail of roughly three hundred pixels wide, so keep it warm white on near black at maximum contrast, unobstructed by any block, shadow or dimension line. No drawn interface elements: no call-to-action buttons, button shapes with text, swipe-up arrows, link chips, cursors, app icons or screen mock-ups; every word lives on a real surface.
